title: The Poisoned Heir of Blackwood Manor
synopsis: Lord Reginald Blackwood was discovered slumped over his desk in his private library during a torrential storm. Three suspects had access to the tea tray, but physical forensics and an alibi contradiction expose the true culprit.
dossier_text:
CASE FILE #1892-BW: DEATH AT BLACKWOOD MANOR
Date: October 24, 1892 | Location: Blackwood Manor, North Riding, Yorkshire
Investigating Officer: Inspector Thomas Vance, Scotland Yard

NARRATIVE BRIEFING:
Lord Reginald Blackwood, 68, wealthy industrialist and philanthropist, was discovered deceased in his locked study at approximately 9:15 PM by the family butler, Higgins. The local practitioner, Dr. Arthur Bell, arrived shortly after to confirm death.

EVIDENCE LOG & WITNESS INTERROGATIONS:
1. Scene Analysis: Lord Reginald sat upright at his mahogany desk. A porcelain teacup of Earl Grey tea was half-empty beside a silver sugar bowl. A faint bitter almond scent was detectable near the rim of the cup.
2. Butler Higgins's Testimony: Higgins served tea to Lord Reginald at 8:00 PM precisely. The tray included hot water, fresh milk, and Demerara sugar cubes. Higgins states: 'I left the tray on the side sideboard in the drawing room for ten minutes between 8:05 and 8:15 while I investigated a loud disturbance in the cellar caused by burst water pipes.'
3. Charles Blackwood (Nephew): Found heavily intoxicated in the billiards room. States he was drinking red Bordeaux from 7:45 PM onward. At 8:15 PM, he knocked over a decanter in the billiards room, which Butler Higgins helped clean up until 8:20 PM.
4. Lady Beatrice Blackwood (Widow): States she was in the second-floor conservatory tending her orchids from 8:00 to 9:00 PM. Admitted she heard footsteps outside the garden path around 8:35 PM.
5. Dr. Arthur Bell (Family Physician): Claimed he only arrived at the manor at 9:05 PM after being summoned for Lord Reginald's chronic heart palpitations, having walked from the village clinic in the heavy storm.
6. Forensic Autopsy & Chemical Analysis: Laboratory testing confirms the victim ingested a lethal dose of potassium cyanide within sugar cubes. The silver sugar tongs tested strongly positive for potassium cyanide residue. No cyanide was detected in the milk or tea leaves.
7. Physical Footprint Corroboration: Fresh footprints with distinctive red peat mud were found leading from the rear estate greenhouse door toward the study window. Red peat soil exists exclusively inside Dr. Bell's botanical greenhouse at the village boundary.
8. Physical Examination of Suspect Belongings: Dr. Bell's riding boots, examined in the cloakroom, were caked in wet, uncleaned red peat mud despite his statement that he walked exclusively along the gravel turnpike road.

evidence_items.title: Autopsy & Toxicology Report
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Extract the exact poison compound, delivery mechanism, and affected items from the forensic autopsy.
evidence_items.description: Coroner report identifying potassium cyanide residue on sugar cubes and silver tongs.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger: TOXICOLOGY FINDINGS: Potassium cyanide poisoning confirmed. Death occurred within 15-20 minutes of ingestion. Lethal coating concentrated specifically on sugar cubes. Tongs tested positive for cyanide residue.

evidence_items.title: Butler Higgins Custody Log
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Extract the timeline of tea preparation and custody, specifically noting when the tray was left unattended.
evidence_items.description: Butler states tea tray sat unattended on drawing room sideboard between 8:05 and 8:15 PM.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger: CUSTODY RECORD: Tea prepared at 8:00 PM. Tray unattended on drawing room sideboard from 8:05 to 8:15 PM due to cellar water pipe emergency.

evidence_items.title: Forensic Trace Analysis: Red Peat Soil
evidence_items.prompt_hint: Extract the soil composition findings and match them against suspect possessions.
evidence_items.description: Red peat mud found at greenhouse rear path matches mud on Dr. Bell's boots.
evidence_items.ocr_ledger: SOIL MATCH: Rare ferruginous red peat mud discovered at garden entrance. Only source in parish is Dr. Arthur Bell's private botanical greenhouse. Dr. Bell's boots tested positive for identical red peat composition.

operational_rules: Forensic Trace Standard §102: Physical forensic corroboration and chemical residue analysis override uncorroborated suspect verbal alibis.
Timeline Discrepancy Principle: Any suspect claiming an arrival time contradicted by physical environmental evidence is considered compromised.

ground_truth.target_rules_or_method: Potassium cyanide coated onto Demerara sugar cubes using silver sugar tongs
ground_truth.target_proof_or_clue: Dr. Bell's boots were caked in red peat mud from the greenhouse path contradicting his 9:05 PM arrival alibi, and cyanide residue was found on the sugar tongs
ground_truth.explanation: Dr. Arthur Bell slipped into the manor during the cellar disturbance (8:05-8:15 PM) via the rear greenhouse path, leaving red peat mud footprints. He applied potassium cyanide to the sugar cubes using the silver sugar tongs. His claim of arriving at 9:05 PM after the storm stopped was directly disproven by the wet red peat mud on his boots.
ground_truth.motive_or_hazard: Financial embezzlement of Lord Reginald's charitable foundation about to be exposed by an impending audit
